title: MASTERS READING ROOM
spans: C 1800 KING KAMEHAMEHA I CONSTRUCTED BRICK HOUSE AT LAHAINA
1823 FIRST AMERICAN MISSIONARIES ARRIVED IN LAHAINA FOR ABOUT A YEAR
1825 KING KAMEHAMEHA II LIVED AT LAHAINA MUCH OF THE TIME
1831 LAHAINALUNA SEMINARY ESTABLISHED FOR TEACHING TEACHERS
1834 LAHAINALUNA PRESS PRODUCED BOOKS IN HAWAIIAN LANGUAGE
1830-60 LAHAINA ANCHORAGE FOR SHIPS PACIFIC WHALING FLEET
1894 MEETING OF FIRST HAWAIIAN CONSTITUTIONAL CONVENTION HERE
1945 ROYAL RESIDENCE AND THE LEGISLATURE MOVED TO HONOLULU

THE TWO-STORY STRUCTURE, COMPLETED IN 1834, WAS BUILT AS A MEETING PLACE FOR USE BY THE OFFICERS OF VISITING SHIPS. THE UPPER AREA WAS THE MASTERS READING ROOM THE LOWER SPACE WAS USED FOR STORAGE, BUILT BY MISSION FUNDS AND CONTRIBUTIONS, THE BUILDING COST A TRIFLE MORE THAN $750. IT WAS IN USE UNTIL 1846 WHEN IT WAS SOLD AT AUCTION AND BECAME A PART OF THE BALDWIN PREMISES. AT PRESENT THE BUILDING IS USED FOR LIVING QUARTERS.

description: The sheet documents the Masters Reading Room in Lahaina, Maui, Hawaii, as part of the Historic American Buildings Survey. It includes a regional map of Maui, a detailed site plan of Lahaina showing street layouts and the building's location near the harbor, and descriptive text blocks outlining the site's history and the building's construction. The text notes the two-story structure was completed in 1834 as a meeting place for visiting ship officers, built with mission funds, and is currently used for living quarters.
